metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity skin throughout. Terracotta marks exactly one thing per beat: the accented move or row, and the verdict's key line. Everything else is warm ink on cream.
metadata.note: Progress update on the week of 2026-11-16 — the second of the week's two videos. Toolkit-only patterns; 16:9 only — progress updates ship landscape-only from week 4 on (user decision, 2026-11-25). Authored after the explainer's GATE V in both cuts: every figure comes from this week's build (PROOF-REVIEW.md pass-1/pass-2 scores, measured audio, clip check, GATE V) or the sources the explainer cites. Claim beats carry a `legibility` contract like the explainer's.

beats.narration: Week twelve progress. This week I rebuilt the Inkling 2 Small teardown as a two-minute audit, and graded it against a written rubric before rendering a single frame. Here's how that went.

props.heading: How the week went

moves.label: READ
moves.detail: 2 config.json files, 2 release posts, 1 paper — every kept number re-checked.

moves.label: AUTHOR
moves.detail: A 12-beat draft for 8 unbuilt Inkling* scenes → 10 beats on 6 patterns.

moves.label: GRADE
moves.detail: PROOF rubric on narration + props, before generating any audio.

moves.label: CHECK
moves.detail: 4K twice; clip lengths asserted, then GATE V on both cuts' frames.

props.keepNote: Move 3 is new this week: the cut is scored against its own standard before the render is spent.

beats.legibility: Each move with its receipt (source count, code count, scores, gate) in the row, revealed as voiced.

beats.narration: The grade, measured. The first cut scored nine of twelve, and failed the production gate: two numbers were voiced before they were readable, and one rubric step never reached the screen. Nine edits later: twelve of twelve, gate passed, before any audio. The bar for these weeks is ten.

beats.narration: What it caught. The summary pattern shows three roadmap cards, so a four-step rubric became three. Two numbers sat in text that fades in late, so they moved up. A computed two ninety-two million became an honest range. And an inferred paper link is now called the nearest paper.

moves.label: ROADMAP
